answer: Admission work is chained rather than pooled: each new seat's puzzle is sealed with the answer of the seat before it, so a household can open only one seat per epoch, and the k-th opening must rework the proofs of all earlier ones. A lone newcomer grinds one puzzle cut from the quartz face and moves on, while a family standing on a single mesa carries the sum of its own history, roughly k-squared work over k epochs for k clones. Every solved chain is stamped as a lotus mark in the public ledger, so an auditor sees one sponsor's marks outgrowing its headcount and traces the household directly.
